name: Airfoil Foundry: an AI-native, owned hot-section casting, coating and repair line for industrial gas turbines (the TSMC of IGT airfoils)
sector: Gas and steam power generation: gas turbine hot-section parts and capacity
one_liner: Build and own the scarce thing in the turbine shortage, a qualified casting, coating and repair line for industrial gas turbine blades and vanes. Use printed ceramic cores and shells and AI solidification control so that one line can run hundreds of reverse-engineered part numbers for 6B, 7EA, 7FA and SGT fleets, and sell parts and repaired sets on long-term supply contracts.
what_it_owns: Three things. (1) The physical capacity: vacuum-induction DS and equiaxed furnaces, ceramic-printing cells, coating booths, braze and HIP, all of it scarce. (2) The frozen, characterised process, a 'PDK' of design rules and process signatures for each alloy and geometry family. (3) A growing library of reverse-engineered technical data packages for orphan and OEM-locked frames. For industrial (non-aviation) turbines there is no FAA or PMA gate. The approver is the asset owner and its insurer, so the company's own evidence record plus customer acceptance is the approval, and it accumulates per part number.
wedge_first_revenue: Months 0-12: hot-gas-path repair and refurbishment on the oldest frames (6B, 7EA, 5002), which needs no casting: AI-planned braze and coating repair, re-tip, recoat, plus reverse-engineered equiaxed nozzles and shrouds produced by partner foundries. Anchor customers are independent service providers and owners of old peakers and resurrection-style fleets, who face OEM parts lead times of 52-80 weeks. First revenue is roughly $2-5M from repaired sets (est.). Months 12-30: commission the first owned equiaxed and DS line using printed cores and shells, which removes the 6-12 month wax and core-die tooling step (est.).
ladder: 1) Repair and refurbish 6B/7EA hot-gas-path sets. 2) Equiaxed stage-2/3 nozzles and buckets from the owned line. 3) DS first-stage buckets for 7EA/7FA. 4) Single-crystal parts for F- and H-class and aeroderivatives. 5) Become the open, characterised 'foundry service' that other designers (new turbine startups, SpaceX-style entrants, the Boom Superpower class) cast into, and the parts supplier to its own turbine fleets.
numbers: Bottleneck: Howmet says it holds more than 50% of the IGT blade market, calls demand 'extraordinary', and says significant new capacity arrives only in 2028-2030 because some equipment takes 2-3+ years (https://www.tikr.com/blog/howmet-aerospace-hwm-stock-drops-elon-musk-turbine-production). One estimate puts a custom DS/SX vacuum-induction furnace at about 1.5 years and purchase order to stable qualified output at 3.5+ years (https://longportapp.cn/topics/39896668). Casting lead times are 52-80 weeks according to a vendor release (https://www.daily-tribune.com/online_features/press_releases/ddm-systems-ceramic-3d-printing-targets-the-gas-turbine-casting-bottleneck-in-ai-data-centers/article_cd7a6cd0-24e0-5113-b0a7-8ffdccc75c12.html). Value of capacity: GE Aerospace agreed to buy Consolidated Precision Products for $11.75B, and SpaceX is building its own blade foundry in Bastrop, TX (https://www.turbomachinerymag.com/view/ge-aerospace-cpp-acquisition-spacex-turbine-blade-foundry). Demand: global turbine orders were 110 GW at end-2025 against 60-70 GW of manufacturing capacity, and turbine prices are heading to about $600/kW by 2027, +195% since 2019 (https://www.power-eng.com/gas/turbines/gas-turbine-prices-climb-195-as-supply-crunch-reshapes-power-development/). Gas turbine services are about $27B in 2025 (https://www.gminsights.com/industry-analysis/gas-turbine-service-market); hot-section parts plus repair are about 30-40% of that, $8-11B (est.). Unit economics (all est.): a 7FA first-stage bucket set costs roughly $1.5-3M from the OEM, and a non-OEM set at 60-70% of OEM price on an owned line runs at 40-50% gross margin. Capital (est.): $5-10M for the repair wedge; $60-150M for the first owned equiaxed/DS line, which is DOE/DPA-fundable as a strategic-capacity case. Time to $100M revenue: about 5-6 years (est.). Ceiling comparables: Howmet (market cap tens of billions, est.), the CPP deal at $11.75B, HEICO, and PCC (sold to Berkshire for $37B in 2016).
ai_role: AI does four jobs. (1) Reverse compilation: CT and blue-light scans, spectroscopy and metallography of worn parts become a TDP with cooling-passage geometry and coating stack. This turns per-part engineering from months into days and makes a library of hundreds of part numbers affordable (P1, P2, P12). (2) A process compiler: physics-informed solidification and grain models plus in-situ thermal and acoustic signatures choose gating, withdrawal rates and core designs, cutting the scrap-and-retry loop that makes casting a 3.5-year ramp (P4, P13). (3) Craft capture: it records master foundry and repair technicians' setups and replays them as procedures and robot motion (P11). (4) An evidence compiler: a per-part digital traveller and a signature-in-envelope acceptance record serve as the qualification package the asset owner and insurer accept.
main_killer: Single-crystal and DS casting yield is tacit, capital-heavy know-how held by three incumbents (Howmet, PCC, and CPP now inside GE). A startup line could take 3.5+ years and $100M+ before it ships qualified parts, and OEMs can threaten LTSA or warranty penalties against owners who install non-OEM hot-section parts.
ai_answer_to_killer: Climb the hardness ladder instead of starting at single-crystal. Repair and equiaxed parts need far less tacit yield knowledge and earn money in year 1. Printed ceramic cores and shells (Lithoz cells are already in Safran production for blade cores, https://www.lithoz.com/en/lithoz-has-installed-cerafab-s65-printers-to-build-casting-parts-for-safran-aircraft-engines/) remove tooling lead time, and AI solidification models plus per-pour signatures compress the learn-by-scrap ramp. Many units per mould and active-learning test design mean each pour is an experiment. The OEM threat does not apply to the target customers: 6B/7EA fleets are mostly out of LTSA, and independent service providers and resurrection fleets want a second source. Industrial turbines have no regulator queue, so the evidence gate is the owner's, and the company can be its own first customer by supplying a sister firm-power fleet.
competitors: Casting: Howmet, PCC Airfoils (Berkshire), CPP (being acquired by GE Aerospace), Doncasters, Chromalloy (Veritas). Repair and independent service providers: Chromalloy, EthosEnergy, PSM (Hanwha), Sulzer, MTU. OEM captive: GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, MHI. New entrants: SpaceX's in-house foundry; DDM Systems (printed ceramic shells); Lithoz and 3DCeram (core printing tools, which are suppliers rather than competitors).
principles_used: P1 (own the frozen target, not the compiler), P3 (owned qualified capacity), P11 (abundant designers, scarce qualified cell), P12 (break the OEM parts lock), P13 (portable recipe plus envelope), P14 (no FAA gate for industrial turbines; owner and insurer are the gate)

score.rationale: Web search budget for this run was used up, so I could not run fresh checks. Scores rest on the cited sources plus prior knowledge: PCC sold for $37B in 2016, the CPP deal is $11.75B, Howmet holds more than 50% of IGT blades, and casting lead times of 52-80 weeks fit what was publicly reported in 2025-26. N: the repair wedge needs only $5-10M and earns money early. The $60-150M line fits DPA/DOE strategic-capacity funding, and non-OEM sets at 60-70% of OEM price with 40-50% gross margin are plausible while the shortage lasts. T: repair revenue arrives in year 1, but the owned line ships qualified parts at month 30 or later and DS parts later still, so $100M in 5-6 years is tight but possible. C: the comparables are among the strongest in hardware (PCC, Howmet, CPP), so 5. A: the hardness ladder (repair, then equiaxed, then DS) plus printed cores, which Lithoz already runs in Safran production, cut the tooling lead time directly. AI solidification control and pour-as-experiment active learning are a plausible answer to the 3.5-year yield ramp. Reverse-compiling TDPs makes a library of hundreds of part numbers affordable. score.biggest_risk: The repair wedge is crowded: Chromalloy, EthosEnergy, PSM and Sulzer already own the 6B/7EA ISP channel. The DS/SX step may still take $150M+ and 4+ years, while Howmet/PCC capacity arrives in 2028-30 and eases the shortage just as the line qualifies.
